title: Punt FG%: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt FG% build, tiered by value, with their volume in PTS, 3PTM and AST? It must explain why FG% swings week to week and why punting one percentage category works well in head-to-head.
summary: Punting FG% suits our 9-cat head-to-head league, because FG% is the category that swings most from game to game and week to week, and chasing both percentages leaves you short elsewhere. Build around high-volume guards and forwards who give points, threes and assists on poor shooting: LaMelo Ball, Trae Young, James Harden, Brandon Miller and Bam Adebayo at the top. Then add cheap value like Derrick White and Damian Lillard, and 1 to 3 USD late picks for threes, blocks and steals.

sections.heading: Why FG% swings week to week

paragraphs.text: FG% is a team ratio: total makes divided by total attempts. Of all the categories, it varies most from game to game and from week to week. FT% varies most from year to year. In a low-volume week each miss moves the ratio more, so the result is close to a coin flip.

In head-to-head, efficiency is the most variable category over a week. One expert prefers steady volume to a small efficiency edge. Good efficiency on low volume barely moves a team ratio. Players with outlier FG% also tend to regress, and a small drop can erase most of their edge. So paying a premium for FG% buys a category you may lose anyway.

sections.heading: Why punting one percentage works in head-to-head

paragraphs.text: Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. Barely winning both is fragile, and the money spent on it leaves you short in other categories. Each week you play one opponent across 9 categories. If you give up FG% on purpose, you aim to win a majority of the other eight.

Because FG% is so swingy, a punt FG% team will still steal the category in some weeks. Meanwhile the players it buys give steady volume in PTS, 3PTM and AST. Many of them also help FT%, so you keep one percentage category instead of punting both.

Several of the core targets also fit a punt TO build: Ball, Young, Harden and Miller. Jalen Green costs little there too. If you lock in two of these early in the auction, think about punting turnovers as well rather than spending to protect them.

Spend most of your early budget on the volume guards. Ball is fair up to the mid 30s USD, since his threes and assists come with no FG% penalty in this build. Young is a round-3 value, and about 33 USD is close to fair. Harden belongs in the low to mid 20s USD, so do not go far past 25 USD. The 42 USD our league paid for him last season is not a guide.

For the frontcourt, Adebayo in the mid 20s USD is the anchor. His 44.6% FG on about 16 attempts is his only weak category. Miller is a third-round value with top-30 upside, and a price between 20 and 26 USD fits. He brings about 3.4 threes, strong FT% and points, but shoots 43% on 16 to 18 shots.

In the middle rounds, Derrick White is the best bargain. Experts value him in the mid 20s USD, so any price near the mid teens is a win. Lillard is a strong value bid at 5 to 10 USD for FT%, threes and assists, because experts value his per-game line at about 20 USD.

Fill the last roster spots at 1 to 3 USD. Myles Turner gives blocks and threes from the center spot and Jabari Smith Jr. gives threes, rebounds and blocks. Jalen Green is cheap for 3PM and PTS, and VanVleet adds threes, assists, steals and low turnovers. Grant, Allen, Herbert Jones and Melton are 1 USD at most, and most of them are better treated as waiver adds.

The experts split on Jerami Grant. The newest expert call says to skip him in 12-team leagues. His profile still allows a 1 USD bid for a punt FG% team that needs about 2.4 threes, 17 points and an 82% FT%, and his 4-4-4 playoff schedule helps. Take him only as your last pick, and only if your build is short on threes.

sections.heading: What to check early and before the playoffs

paragraphs.text: In the first weeks, check minutes and usage before anything else, because this build lives on volume. Ball should reach about 32 minutes. Young needs 33 or more minutes and double-digit assists. Harden should stay near 33 minutes. Lillard needs 30 or more minutes, and Green needs 30 or more minutes while really running the point. If a late flyer like Allen or Melton does not win a starting spot, drop him quickly.

Also watch for FG% recovering. White back above 40% and Turner recovering from 44% would make them better all-round players and raise their trade value. Young falling back to about 42% does not matter to you, but it may lower his value to other managers.

Plan for weeks 19 to 21 before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline. Miami has only 10 games in those weeks, and so does VanVleet's Houston. Houston's schedule there is 3-3-4, which also hurts Jabari Smith Jr. Ball has a two-game week (week of March 15) and Harden has a two-game finals week. Portland has three back-to-backs, so check whether Lillard plays them. Grant's 4-4-4 is the best schedule in this group. Trade the short-schedule players for volume on stronger schedules if you can.
